name: What is the difference between a curbless shower and a low-threshold shower?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a curbless shower and a low-threshold shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Walk-in showers can be designed with a low-profile threshold or completely curbless (barrier-free). Curbless showers eliminate tripping hazards, making them ideal for aging-in-place or accessibility modifications, but they require recessing the subfloor or sloping the entire shower pan to ensure water drains properly. Low-threshold showers retain a small lip (typically two to four inches) that makes water containment simpler and reduces framing adjustments. The right choice depends on your long-term mobility requirements, bathroom layout, and whether your floor joists allow for recessed pan construction without major structural reconfiguration.
acceptedAnswer.description: Curbless showers sit flush with the bathroom floor for seamless accessibility, while low-threshold showers use a small curb to contain water with minimal structural adjustments.
